shard_sizing_comparison.cascades_compared: cash_print_sheets_queue (5 leaves, 4 shards) vs cash_print_tunnel_push (4 leaves, 1 shard) vs cash_plugin_distribution (2 leaves, 1 shard) -- same repo, same overlord, overlapping impl files, 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-19
shard_sizing_comparison.headline_quote: 'The 4-shard run cost roughly 4x the audit overhead for the same admission outcome.' -- leandrc49__shard-sizing-ab file
shard_sizing_comparison.same_file_same_result: 'scripts/build_cash_workflow.mjs (4200 lines)' was leaf-01's target in both sheets_queue (dedicated shard-a, alone) and tunnel_push (shared shard with 3 other leaves). 'The single writer handled it, and the single auditor returned green on leaf-01's goal fidelity. Same file, same size, both configurations, same result.'
shard_sizing_comparison.what_more_shards_bought: 'Nothing that the shared context wouldn't have produced, and one thing they actively cost. Zero cross-shard findings ... each of the four auditors saw only its own shard's tests against its own shard's brief. Four auditors produce four blind spots between them.'
shard_sizing_comparison.cross_leaf_defect_only_surfaced_in_the_s: 'The one genuinely cross-leaf defect came from the only shard holding two leaves.' (shard-c-printjobs-unit-mismatch, leaf-03 vs leaf-04 unit inconsistency) -- 'Two leaves, one context, one finding. Split them and nothing in the run sees it.'
shard_sizing_comparison.single_shard_produced_a_cross_leaf_obser: tunnel_push's single auditor flagged 'leaf-02's 3 impl_files have no in-repo call relationship' -- 'a statement about the shape of one leaf's decomposition that only reads as a finding when you hold the others alongside it.'
shard_sizing_comparison.skill_rule_gap_identified: check_invariants.check_shard_sizing only fails a shard holding TOO MANY leaves, never a wave split into too many shards: '5 leaves / 4 shards -> PASS (no finding); 7 leaves / 1 shard -> FAIL: 7 leaves in one shard.' Recommended fix quoted: 'invert the default. One shard, unless a stated trigger fires ... make check_shard_sizing two-sided so shards > ceil(leaves / cap) fails the Phase 3 audit the same way under-sharding does.'
shard_sizing_comparison.conclusion: On this evidence, splitting a small (4-6 leaf) wave into multiple shards did not increase finding count or quality -- it produced zero cross-shard findings, cost ~4x the audit overhead, and the one real cross-leaf defect found in the whole comparison came specifically from the shard that was NOT split (the 2-leaf shard-c). More shards = smaller per-auditor context = more blind spots between auditors, not fewer.

false_positives_or_ineffective_fixes.description: The auditor's 'bug' finding (test never asserts returncode==0 despite its name claiming it) was factually accurate about the assertion gap, but the fix it implicitly called for (add returncode==0) would have made the test WRONG, because the script legitimately cannot guarantee exit 0 given an unreachable DATABASE_URL (confirmed by a sibling test file's own comment). The parent's actual fix was a rename only -- no assertion was added or changed. This is the corpus's one clear case of an auditor finding needing an overlord override rather than a straight fix-as-suggested.

notes: INDEX.md's own stated purpose for this corpus: to compare 'what the pre-auditor process actually caught (via TDD side-effects and manual admission-time diff review only) against what Phase 3.4 catches pre-impl' -- this file (post-auditor-narrative.json) covers only the WITH-auditor side; no direct pre/post comparison is computed here.

Only 3 of 9 originally-scanned projects had any post-cutoff manager-mode activity (the-best-salesmen, leandrc49, switchboard) -- this is a small, non-random sample of production cascades, not a systematic trial.

Two of the six sub-cascades in the leandrc49 file (cash_print_sheets_queue in its cash-print-cascades framing, cash_print_tunnel_push, cash_plugin_distribution) have no surviving/detailed TEST-AUDIT artifact in the primary run-dump file; some of that gap is partially filled by the separate shard-sizing-ab file, which is explicitly a cross-run comparison document, not a run dump, and only reports findings relevant to the shard-count question.

No cascade in this corpus reports a case where a fix prompted by the auditor was later shown to be simply wrong (i.e., the auditor's finding held up in every case except switchboard's bug-finding, where the finding's factual premise was correct but its implied remedy was not).

Brief-dialect (inlined TEST-AUDIT-BRIEF vs path-list) is not discussed in any of the four detail files or INDEX.md; all cascades are noted only as test_owned_by: parent throughout, which is a different axis (test authorship) from brief dialect.

Category vocabulary gap: three of the corpus's most narratively significant 'slipped past' items (implementation-code leak into shipped output, staging/isolation-discipline violations, shared-harness bugs found only at runtime) do not fit any category in CATEGORY_VOCAB.md, because the vocabulary is scoped to test-content defects and these are not test-content defects -- they are implementation-time or process-discipline failures that a pre-spawn test-quality auditor is structurally unable to reach. This is itself a finding worth surfacing to Agora rather than forcing a fit.
